title: SC PSC Order No. 2026-155H — Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Confidential Treatment - Application of CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc. for Designation as an Eligible Telecommunications Carrier in the State of South Carolina
summary: Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Granting Confidential Treatment - Application of CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc. for Designation as an Eligible Telecommunications Carrier in the State of South Carolina
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF SOUTH CAROLINA 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE 

DOCKET NO. 2021-15-C ORDER NO. 2026-155-H 

JULY 7, 2026 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER: C. Jo Anne Wessinger Hill, Esquire 

DOCKET DESCRIPTION: DOCKET NO. 2021-15-C – Application of CarolinaConnect 
Cooperative, Inc. for Designation as an Eligible Telecommunications Carrier in the State of South 
Carolina 

MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION: Request by CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc. 
(CarolinaConnect) for the Commission to grant Confidential Treatment of its Annual Eligible 
Telecommunications Carrier Report required to be filed with the Commission, along with the 
attached copy of its filed FCC Form 481 designated as Exhibit A in the annual Report. This 
Request was filed on June 24, 2026 (Request). 

HEARING OFFICER’S ACTION: This matter comes before the Hearing Officer on the 
Request of CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc. (CarolinaConnect), seeking Confidential Treatment 
for its annual Eligible Telecommunications Carrier Report (ETC Report) required to be filed with 
the Commission, along with the attached copy of its filed FCC Form 481 which was included as 
Exhibit A to the ETC Report. This Request, along a copy of the information filed under seal, was 
filed on June 24, 2026, with a redacted public version. 

The Request is made pursuant to the South Carolina Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. 
§§ 30-4-10, et. seq., and S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804(S)(2). The Request is also in compliance 
with Commission Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-490, 2023-859, and 2025-321. In its request for 
confidential treatment, CarolinaConnect identified and designated the confidential information 
which it maintains to be proprietary, highly sensitive, and confidential. Request, p. 1. 

In submitting the Request, CarolinaConnect asserts the need to protect the redacted information 
from public disclosure because the confidential information is proprietary and of a commercially 
sensitive nature. The identified and designated information is confidential information that is not 
known, or available, to the public or the company’s competitors. If the information is publicly 
disclosed, CarolinaConnect will be competitively harmed from such disclosure and risk other 
carriers obtaining information not publicly known or available. In fact, public disclosure of such 
highly confidential information would allow competitors to obtain economic value from such 
disclosure. CarolinaConnect also asks for the Commission to exclude this information from public 
disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10, et. seq. 

Commission Regulation 103-804(S)(2) provides that the Commission, within its discretion, can 
determine what matters are placed and available in the public record on the Commission’s Docket 
Management System (DMS). S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804(S)(2) (2012). Likewise, the 
Commission has discretion to determine what matters are exempt from public disclosure, including 
exemption from release under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et. seq. 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE NO. 2026-155-H 
JULY 7, 2026 
PAGE 2 OF 2 

Disclosure of confidential and proprietary information can cause competitive harm to a company 
when such information is not available to the public. Considering the Request of CarolinaConnect 
Cooperative, Inc., and its actions in compliance with Commission Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-
490, 2023-859, and applicable laws, the Hearing Officer finds and concludes that confidential 
treatment is warranted: 

(1) for the proprietary and commercially sensitive information identified and marked by 
CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., as confidential in the filing of its annual Eligible 
Telecommunications Carrier Report and the attached copy of its filed FCC Form 481 
which is included as Exhibit A in the annual ETC Report. 

Accordingly, the Request for Confidential Treatment is granted as requested by 
CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., for the information and data designated as confidential 
in its annual ETC Report and the attached copy of its filed FCC Form 481 included as 
Exhibit A to the annual ETC Report. 

The Hearing Officer further finds and concludes that the non-redacted confidential version of its 
annual ETC Report and the FCC Form 481 filed by CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., are exempt 
from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et. seq. 
Therefore, the Request is granted to exempt the information designated as confidential in the 
annual ETC Report and in the FCC Form 481 filed by CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., from 
disclosure pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act. 

The Commission shall maintain as confidential and/or exempt from disclosure under the Freedom 
of Information Act the non-redacted confidential designated version of certain information 
identified and marked as confidential and proprietary by CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., in its 
annual ETC Report and in the FCC Form 481 unless or until the Commission rules designated and 
identified information is not entitled to protection from public disclosure, or CarolinaConnect 
Cooperative, Inc., agrees that such information is no longer confidential, commercially sensitive, 
or proprietary. 

On behalf of the Commission, this Hearing Officer further accepts for filing both the nonredacted 
confidential version filed under seal and the redacted public version of the annual Eligible 
Telecommunications Carrier Report and the attached copy of the filed FCC Form 481 included 
with the Report as Exhibit A as filed with the Commission by CarolinaConnect Cooperative, Inc., 
in this Docket. 

This concludes the Hearing Officer’s Directive.
